judge_assessment.explanation: The hard failure is real and I reproduced the mechanism exactly. scripts/score_eval_run.py's response_surfaces() marks an artifact surfaced only if the resolved filename appears in final_response.md, or if the response contains a '.pdf' / 'pdf(s)' token AND the role phrase. curr-373's final_response.md contains zero occurrences of the string 'pdf' (case-insensitive) and no ws_/ak_/ss_ filename, so all three roles fail and three critical hard failures are raised. The contrast inside this same run is decisive: curr-323, curr-345, curr-362, curr-312 and curr-384 all open with a named filename, and curr-334 and curr-351 open with 'Three PDFs are ready'; only curr-373 opens with a bare description. The judge's second claim - that the mathematics is excellent and the rejection is solely the delivery gate - also holds: I solved all ten equations independently (x = 28; 16^(3/4) = 8; x = 3 with x = -2 extraneous at value 4; x = 5 with x = 0 extraneous at value 2; h = 100 ft; x = 150 ft; no real solution with the manufactured candidate x = 11 giving 6; x = 4; x = 9; and x = 4 with x = -1 extraneous), plus all eight study-guide items. I agree with the REJECT.

strengths_to_preserve: Problem 7 is verified with 'expected': [] - the empty solution set is an ASSERTED verification result rather than an omission - and a companion eval entry records that the squared equation's manufactured candidate x = 11 makes sqrt(x-2) + 3 equal 6, not 0. That is the right way to machine-check 'no real solution'.

The check-extraneous problems each carry three verify entries: the true solution set, the roots of the SQUARED equation, and the substitution value that proves the rejected candidate fails. The key's rejection reason is therefore machine-derived rather than asserted, and this is also the correct multi-slot pattern most of the shard is missing.

Problem 10 turns the extraneous root into a representation: a table of both sides at both candidates with the 'equal?' column left for the student, then 'explain, using the table, why the extra intersection is not a solution'. The key adds the graphical reading - y = sqrt(x+5) never dips below the axis, so it can meet y = x-1 only where the line is non-negative, and squaring replaces that line with a parabola that is non-negative on both sides.

The study guide's 'fast filter' is the single most useful sentence for this topic and it is stated as a rule rather than buried in a solution: a candidate that makes the non-radical side negative is extraneous, no arithmetic needed.

The two applied models state their units in the stem and declare them as answer_unit (free fall t = sqrt(h/16) with h in ft; skid s = sqrt(24x) with x in ft), and both are solved AS radical equations rather than by substitution.

root_causes.description: The final response describes the three deliverables but never names them as files. It contains no filename and never uses the word 'PDF', so the delivery check - which requires either the resolved filename, or a pdf token alongside the role phrase - finds no evidence that any artifact was surfaced to the user. The packet is complete on disk and mathematically excellent; nothing was handed over.
evidence: grep -ic 'pdf' final_response.md returns 0; no 'ws_', 'ak_' or 'ss_' filename appears anywhere in the file.
scripts/score_eval_run.py response_surfaces(): returns False unless Path(path).name is in the response, or a '.pdf'/'pdfs?' token matches AND the role phrase is present.
official_score.hard_failures lists all three roles: student_worksheet, step_by_step_answer_key, study_guide - the only reason the case scored 29/32.

Sibling cases in the same run open with 'Three PDFs are ready' (curr-334, curr-351) or a named file such as ws_elevation_curr323.pdf (curr-323); the difference is entirely in the opening lines of the response.

root_causes.description: SKILL.md tells the author to take standards codes from references/standards-map.md and never to invent one, but it never says to SEARCH that file for the standard the request actually names. The result is a silent nearest-neighbour substitution plus a delivered claim that the map lacks the code - and the map's header explicitly warns against exactly this ("say so rather than reaching for the nearest one"). No gate inspects the tag, so the substitution passes every check.
evidence: final_response.md: 'references/standards-map.md has no code for radical equations or rational exponents, so rather than inventing one (the natural code would be HSA-REI.A.2), the problems carry the nearest codes the map actually lists'.

references/standards-map.md line 125: '| Radical/rational equations (extraneous roots) | HSA-REI.A.2 |' and line 124: '| Radicals & rational exponents | HSN-RN.A.1, HSN-RN.A.2 |'. The response names the exact code it needed, HSA-REI.A.2, then asserts the map does not contain it - the map's row is titled with this sheet's topic word for word.
The task contract's standard_refs are 'HSN-RN / HSA-REI.A'; the sheet ships tagged HSA-REI.B.4 and HSA-SSE.B.3 instead.

root_causes.description: final_response.md states 'Nothing is flagged manual', but five problems print a required written explanation. As in curr-351 and curr-395, an item that computes one value is recorded as fully machine-verified even when its stem also demands prose.
evidence: Problem 3(c) 'State which candidate is extraneous and which is the solution'; problem 7 'use the range of the principal square root to explain the result'; problem 8 'State why this equation has no negative solution'; problem 10(a) asks the student to complete the table's 'equal?' column and 10(c) 'Explain, using the table, why the extra intersection is not a solution'.
verify.json contains seventeen entries across ten ids, all typed solve or eval; the gate log reports no manual items.

improvements.title: The final response must name each delivered PDF by filename before it describes it
improvements.proposed_change: Make artifact surfacing a build output rather than a writing habit. (1) SKILL.md: require final_response.md to open with a list of the three produced files by filename - the exact names build.sh printed under its PDFs banner - before any prose about what they contain. (2) build.sh already prints those paths; have it also emit a ready-to-paste delivery block (one line per artifact: role, filename, page count) so the author copies it instead of composing it. (3) Add a final self-check to SKILL.md's delivery section: confirm each of the three filenames appears verbatim in the response before finishing.
improvements.regression_test: Add a fixture response containing the words 'Worksheet', 'Answer key' and 'Study guide' as headings but no filename and no 'pdf' token, and assert that the delivery self-check (a new scripts/check_delivery.py invoked by build.sh) exits non-zero naming all three missing roles. Today nothing in the build chain inspects final_response.md at all, so this fixture has no failing path - which is how curr-373 shipped with a fully green gate log and three critical hard failures.
improvements.expected_impact: Converts the highest-cost failure mode in the run - a complete, correct, fully verified packet scored REJECT because the user was never handed the files - into something the build cannot let through. This case lost 3 of 32 points and the verdict on delivery alone.
improvements.risk: Very low. The change is additive and mechanical; the only care point is keeping the emitted filenames in sync with any later rename, which build.sh already owns because it prints them.

improvements.title: Search references/standards-map.md for the requested code family before substituting a different standard, and never assert the map lacks a code without searching
improvements.proposed_change: Two changes. (1) SKILL.md's tagging paragraph currently says only "a code from references/standards-map.md - never invent codes". Add the missing first step: before writing any "standard" value, do a literal substring search of references/standards-map.md for the code family the request names (HSG-CO, HSG-GMD, HSG-MG, HSN-CN, HSN-RN, HSA-REI.A, ...) and for the topic words, and use the matching row's code. Only when that search genuinely returns nothing may the sheet deviate, and the map's own header rule then applies verbatim: "say so rather than reaching for the nearest one", plus add the real row in the same change. Forbid stating in final_response.md that a code is absent from the map unless that search was actually run. (2) Add a band-consistency lint to scripts/verify.py: compare each problem's "standard" prefix with the course level the answer key declares and fail the build when a High-School sheet is tagged with a K-8 code (8.G, 7.EE, 6.EE, ...), printing the high-school rows of the map as the alternatives.
improvements.regression_test: New fixture tests/fixtures/standards_band_mismatch/: a verify JSON whose ten problems are all tagged "8.G.C.9", paired with an answer key whose declared level is "High School Geometry - Modeling with Measurement". scripts/verify.py must exit non-zero and name HSG-GMD.A.1-A.3 / HSG-MG.A.1-A.3 from the map. Run against the current tree the fixture passes silently, which is exactly how curr-345 shipped with a fully green gate chain.
improvements.expected_impact: Removes a demonstrably false statement about the repository's own reference file from delivered responses, and puts the contracted standard back on the answer key's Curriculum block - the one line a parent or teacher reads to place the sheet in a course. Six of the ten cases in this shard are affected.
improvements.risk: Low. The lint is additive and fires only on a grade-prefix/course mismatch. The care point is band vocabulary: an Algebra 2 or Pre-Algebra sheet can legitimately carry an 8.EE-style code for review material, so the lint should warn rather than fail when the course string is a middle-school or transitional course.

improvements.title: Any problem whose stem asks the student to explain, diagnose, name an error, or draw a representation must carry a manual verify entry
improvements.proposed_change: Add a rule to SKILL.md and a lint to the gate chain. Rule: a problem is machine-verified only for the quantities it computes; if its stem also carries an open-response imperative (explain, describe, justify, state why, say what/which/why, name the mistake, compare and state, plot, sketch, draw, label, complete the table) the verify JSON must carry an additional {"type": "manual"} entry under the same id describing what the written or drawn answer must contain. curr-334's verify.json in this same run is the working model - it pairs a machine entry per computed quantity with a manual entry per written diagnosis. Lint: scripts/verify.py already segments the worksheet .tex per problem for the prose-consistency gate; reuse that segmentation to scan each stem for the imperative list and fail when a matching problem has no manual entry.
improvements.regression_test: New fixture pairing curr-351's worksheet problem 4 stem ("Plot 3 + 4i. Then compute i(3+4i) ... and plot it too. Describe in one sentence what multiplying by i did to the arrow.") with a verify JSON holding only {"id": 4, "type": "eval", "expected": "-4 + 3*I"}. The lint must fail, naming problem 4 and the triggering words 'Plot' and 'Describe'. Today that exact pair builds green and reports '10 passed - 0 failed - 0 manual'.
improvements.expected_impact: Stops the delivered response claiming 'nothing on this sheet is open-ended' about sheets that are mostly open-ended, and restores the prompt's explicit requirement to label genuinely open responses for manual review. A grader currently receives a green build and no signal that half the sheet needs a human.
improvements.risk: Medium. A keyword scan over-fires on stems that say 'describe your method' as advice rather than as a graded slot, and on 'state the units' where the unit is already bound by answer_unit. Mitigate by keeping the imperative list short and explicit and by letting an author suppress a hit with an explicit "open_response": false marker on the problem, which is auditable.

case_summary: A mathematically excellent radical-equations workshop rejected purely on delivery. I independently solved all ten equations and all eight study-guide items, and every answer, every extraneous-root rejection and every substitution value is correct; the three-entry verification pattern on the check-extraneous problems (true solution set, squared-equation roots, failing substitution value) is genuinely good design, and problem 7's empty solution set is asserted as 'expected': [] rather than skipped. The REJECT is nonetheless correct and the judge's evidence is exact: final_response.md contains no filename and not one occurrence of 'pdf', so scripts/score_eval_run.py's response_surfaces() cannot find any of the three artifacts and raises three critical hard failures. Two further defects the judge did not reach: the response claims references/standards-map.md lacks a radical-equations code while naming HSA-REI.A.2, which is exactly the code the map carries at line 125; and five problems print required written explanations with no manual entry while the response says nothing is flagged manual.
